purpose: Part 7 of the final zero-cost compiler gate: text-only review of every community_gathering row's actual rendered scene text, to check whether the weak_extrapolation grammar produces plausible object-first scenes or loses hobby identity. No image generated or inspected.

rows.title: Founder Meetups
rows.note: Generic professional-meetup grammar (shared table, communal materials) fits plausibly; identity carried adequately by title context.

rows.title: Startup Meetups
rows.note: Same as founder_meetups - generic professional-meetup fit.

rows.title: Tech Meetups
rows.note: Same as founder_meetups - generic professional-meetup fit.

rows.title: Book Swaps
rows.note: The grammar's 'communal objects and shared materials' phrasing is generic enough that it does not explicitly evoke books; plausible the model renders books (matches a book-swap table image search prior) but the specific hobby identity is carried more weakly than the professional-meetup rows. Not reclassified this round - flagged for the future 16-card visual test rather than forced to a bespoke sub-grammar, since it is not clearly nonsensical (unlike car_meets/repair_workshops below).

rows.title: Clothing Swaps
rows.note: Same concern as book_swaps - generic 'shared materials' language doesn't explicitly evoke clothing/racks/piles. Flagged, not fixed this round.

rows.title: Car Meets
rows.note: The original community_gathering_traces grammar (shared table, chairs, food, decorations 'warmly prepared for togetherness') was genuinely nonsensical for a car meet - confirmed by reading the actual rendered scene text. Fixed via a new id-exact override routing to a new community_gathering_vehicles rule (generic unbranded vehicles parked together, no owners/drivers/spectators). protagonist_type changed from environment to machine_process. Still weak_extrapolation - not visually tested.

rows.title: Repair Workshops
rows.note: The communal-table/food/decoration tone genuinely mismatches a repair workshop's tools/craft identity - confirmed by reading the actual rendered scene text. Fixed via a new id-exact override rerouting it out of community_gathering_traces entirely to generic_structural_containment (arranged tools, natural wear, activity mid-progress), which fits a workshop far better. protagonist_type changed from environment to object. Still weak_extrapolation - not visually tested.

honesty_note: Per the task's explicit instruction ('honesty over forcing 0'), book_swaps and clothing_swaps are NOT claimed as fully resolved. They are not nonsensical the way car_meets and repair_workshops were (which is why those two got a real fix this round), but their hobby-identity strength under the generic grammar is genuinely uncertain without a visual test. Recommendation: if a future community_gathering visual test shows these two rendering generically (unidentifiable as book/clothing swaps specifically), add bespoke id overrides for them the same way car_meets and repair_workshops were fixed this round, rather than trusting the generic grammar indefinitely.
